authorization_reference: User-authorized single RTX5090; CONDITIONAL pilot after warm-cache A/A analysis. Same frozen H128, capacity victim enabled, Q1/Q10 differ only in post-first-output protection. Q10 extends only with known native R=0, pure decode, no pending load, and sufficient future block growth budget; changed/unknown conditions fall back. Both arms get the same seed cache in independent copies and identical sparse new telemetry. Primary question: do actual safe extensions yield more outputs before next native preemption and what are complete-request target/peer costs? Require full cohort, actual extension-to-output chains and complete release-to-completion follow-up. No zero-action efficacy claim. Favorable exploration requires output rate >=97%, mean flow <=105%, lower max gap versus matched Q1, preserving per-request losses and all failed/uncompleted requests; one ordered pair is not confirmation. 900s/cell,3200s/group,90GiB cgroup,existing common nonblocking lock. No parameter or seed rescue.
